chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from 'Abd al-A'la, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whoever travels to this House as a pilgrim or one performing Umrah, free from arrogance, will return from his sins as he was on the day his mother gave birth to him.'
Then whoever hastens off in two days, there is no sin on him, and whoever remains behind, there is no sin on him, (this is) the one who fears.

I said, 'What is arrogance?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The greatest of arrogance is contempt for the people and foolishness regarding the truth.' I said, 'What is contempt for the people and foolishness regarding the truth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He disregards the truth and slanders its people; and whoever does that, disputes with Allah regarding His cloak.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of arrogance (al-kibr) in Shia hadith and how does it affect Hajj?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links the spiritual efficacy of Hajj to the purification of the ego, specifically defining 'al-kibr' (arrogance) not merely as pride, but as the active rejection of truth and disparagement of its adherents. This interpretation aligns with the Shia exegetical tradition where 'disputing with Allah’s cloak' signifies a direct challenge to divine authority and grace, emphasizing that ritual correctness must be accompanied by moral humility to achieve the promised state of sinlessness.
